text:
Situation: Tobramycin sulfate injection is listed by FDA as To Be Discontinued. FDA's shortage list records that Hospira, Inc., a Pfizer Company, discontinued manufacture with an initial posting date of 2026-07-17. There is no current FDA shortage signal for tobramycin at the plants supplying Corvale East or Corvale General. Corvale East holds 893 units at 29.8 units per day, providing 30 days on hand. Corvale General holds 551 units at 32.5 units per day, providing 17 days on hand. Stock detail: Corvale East TOBRAMYCIN 300MG/5ML 5ML AMP 354 on hand, 24.5 days; Corvale East TOBRAMYCIN 300MG/4ML 4ML AMP 539 on hand, 35 days; Corvale General Tobramycin 293.83 on hand, 18.4 days; Corvale General tobramycin 257.14 on hand, 15.6 days.

Why (FDA record): FDA's shortage list shows Hospira, Inc., a Pfizer Company, discontinued manufacture of tobramycin sulfate injection with an initial posting date of 2026-07-17.

Our position: Current inventory covers near-term use at both sites. No active shortage signal exists for our supplying plants. Secondary suppliers are not on FDA's shortage list today, but their labels name no plant we could verify.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to evaluate and qualify secondary suppliers A-S Medication Solutions, Advanced Rx Pharmacy of Tennessee LLC, Alembic Pharmaceuticals Inc., Alembic Pharmaceuticals Limited, and American Health Packaging; requires P&T committee approval before purchase.
2. Buyer to monitor FDA shortage list weekly for new signals affecting our supplying plants; requires pharmacy director approval.
3. Buyer to report inventory days on hand to pharmacy director every 7 days; requires pharmacy director acknowledgment.

Not recommended: Initiate therapeutic alternatives or protocol changes at this time.
